newsitem.title: USA: ConEd boosts NY power output to skirt line outage.
newsitem.headline: ConEd boosts NY power output to skirt line outage.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co (ConEd) said Monday it switched on more power units in southern New York to make up for the loss of power usually carried to New York City on a key line that was shut last month.
The need for activating the units was also partly caused by the loss of the 975 megawatt (MW) Indian Point 2 nuclear power plant, which was shut last Thursday for refueling.
"We put on both the Roseton and Bowline plants which we have part shares in," a company spokesman said .
He said ConEd today is receiving 396 MW of power from the 605 MW Bowline Point natural gas-fired unit 2 and 235 MW from 599 MW Roseton oil-fired unit 2.
The utility also turned on the 490 MW gas-fired unit 3 at its Arthur Kill power plant, he added.
ConEd brought into service the adjoining 345 MW Arthur Kill unit 2 last week.

A 345 kilovolt (KV) Gilboa-Leeds high-voltage line was damaged by a loose equipment part and out of service last month. The cable runs between substations in the New York towns of Leeds and Pleasant Valley over the Hudson River.
A parallel 345 KV line on Gilboa-Leeds system was unaffected, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp (NIMO) said.
NIMO the operator has not decided when the damaged power line will return to service, a NIMO spokesman said.
The Bowline and Roseton units, located south of the Leeds and Pleasant Valley substations, do not need the Gilboa-Leeds transmission line to move power into New York City, a ConEd spokesman said.
The length of time that the Roseton, Bowline and Arthur Kill units remain in service would depend on the energy demand on ConEd's system, he said.
